title: When the Ledger Wakes
premise: In the winter of 1919, in a river town whose only bridge has closed for the season, Jude Okafor — apprentice to a mapmaker who died surveying the disputed borderlands — must finish the master's atlas while the town's occupying garrison and the returning enemy delegation both want the maps for themselves. Bound by a promise made in peacetime to Tomas, the son of the rival cartographer now declared an enemy, Jude smuggles him into the map house and hides him through the frozen months, falling in love as the armistice negotiations stall. When the garrison discovers the atlas contains evidence that would redraw the border and condemn the town, Jude must choose between delivering the finished atlas to duty or burning it to save Tomas. In the end Jude surrenders the maps but keeps one page back — the master's true border, drawn in water-soluble ink — letting the truth wash away rather than let it kill, and crosses the reopened bridge with Tomas as spring breaks.
about_author: Coral Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime cartography collections before turning to fiction. They write historical novels about the people history forgets to name on its maps.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Opening the dead master's studio, Jude confronts the unfinished atlas and the promise made at the funeral: finish it before the bridge reopens. Establishes the town, the garrison, and Jude's belief that history happens elsewhere. Emotional beat: grief braided with quiet ambition.

chapters.title: Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The final day before the seasonal bridge closure; the town rushes its last trade, and among the departing travelers Jude glimpses Tomas, who mouths a word Jude pretends not to see. The bridge chains rattle shut behind them. Beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Dead Man's Hand
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Cataloguing the master's papers, Jude finds discrepancies between the official border and the surveyed one — and a sealed letter addressed to 'the one who finishes this.' First appearance of Major Voss, who requisitions the studio. Beat: unease sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Garrison Takes an Interest
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The major reviews the atlas commission and realizes what the border pages could justify; he orders Jude supervised 'for their protection.' Introduces Sergeant Ilsa Brandt, assigned as Jude's shadow. Beat: the trap closing politely.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Dark
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Weeks into winter, someone scratches at the loading door: Tomas, half-frozen, having crossed the ice after his father was arrested as an enemy agent. Jude remembers the peacetime promise and lets him in. Beat: terror and tenderness in the same breath.

chapters.title: Two Cartographers' Children
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Hidden in the map drawers' loft, Tomas explains his father's arrest and the letter both masters exchanged years ago. He and Jude argue about whether the atlas is salvation or weapon. Beat: old friendship tested by new politics.

chapters.title: Sergeant Brandt's Rounds
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa inspects the studio, notices flour bought for two, says nothing — yet. Her own war losses make her sympathetic but dangerous. Beat: suspense of almost-discovery, complicated by unexpected kinship.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude opens the master's sealed letter: instructions to hide the true border pages if war comes, because 'a line drawn in ink becomes a grave dug in advance.' Jude begins copying the atlas with altered borders for the garrison. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Feast of the Frozen River
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, mostly Tomas's POV. The town's midwinter festival; Jude and Tomas slip out together under festival noise, dance once in the square, nearly get caught by Ilsa. Beat: love blooming against curfew, joy edged with guilt.

chapters.title: What Voss Wants
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss reveals to Ilsa that the armistice delegation arrives when the bridge reopens, and the atlas will be presented as evidence; he suspects the master falsified surveys and wants proof. Beat: stakes clarified — the atlas can condemn a whole valley.

chapters.title: The Price of Flour
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa confronts Jude privately, not with arrest but a bargain: she'll stay silent if Jude shows her whether the master's border is true, because her brother died holding a line drawn by men like these. Beat: ally or informant — impossible to tell.

chapters.title: Copying by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Jude and Tomas alternating POV. Working nights, they forge the garrison's copy while preserving the true plates; hands touch over the drafting table; first kiss amid compass arcs. Beat: intimacy fused with conspiracy.

chapters.title: Arrest at the Mill
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas ventures out for medicine and is recognized; he escapes, but the garrison now knows an enemy fugitive hides in town. Voss locks down the quarter. Beat: the noose tightening around the map house.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Choice
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ordered to search the studio thoroughly, Ilsa finds Tomas's boot prints in the loft dust — and burns the evidence instead, telling Voss the trail leads to the mill district. Beat: her defection from duty to conscience, paid for with fear.

chapters.title: The Master's Grave
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude visits the master's grave to decide, and meets the old ferryman who carried the master's last survey trip; learns the true border would give the valley to neither side but split it — ruin either way. Beat: the terrible arithmetic of truth.

chapters.title: Armistice Rumors
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Word comes that the delegation may sign without inspecting the valley — unless Voss presents the atlas. He moves to seize the originals ahead of schedule. Beat: countdown begun; antagonist fully committed.

chapters.title: Night Raid on the Map House
chapters.summary: Jude and Tomas POV, interleaved. Soldiers arrive early; Ilsa delays them at the gate; Jude and Tomas flee across rooftops with the true plates, hiding in the icehouse. Beat: pure chase tension, found family holding under pressure.

chapters.title: What the Ink Is For
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Trapped in the icehouse, Jude and Tomas fight over the endgame: deliver truth and doom the valley, or destroy it and betray the master. Tomas offers to surrender himself so Jude can hand over a clean atlas. Beat: love against duty at full collision.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens Early
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Engineers break the ice early; the delegation will cross within days. Ilsa gives Jude her uniform pass and tells them the price she already paid. Beat: sacrifice passed like a relay baton.

chapters.title: Water-Soluble
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, climax. Before the delegation, Jude presents the atlas — minus one page — while Voss demands the missing plate. Jude reveals the master's final border was drawn in soluble ink and lets the river water take it: no line, no grave. Voss's case collapses; Tomas walks free under armistice amnesty. Beat: catharsis through refusal.

chapters.title: Signatures
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Jude's POV. The armistice is signed without the valley's condemnation; Voss is recalled in disgrace; Ilsa chooses to stay as the town's constable. The master's blank page is reframed in the studio — an honest emptiness. Beat: bittersweet justice, debts acknowledged.

chapters.title: Crossing in Spring
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The bridge reopens; Jude and Tomas cross together toward the capital to apprentice under a neutral academy, carrying the master's tools. Final image: drawing new maps where every line is labeled 'provisional.' Beat: hope earned, survival priced, love chosen.
